summary.intent: Run a staged, read-only quality sweep of the caliper repo (Phase 0 scanner first, then agent phases) while concurrently landing trail 192, a collapse-by-relevance change for dependency prop sources, with its measurement branch.
summary.outcome: Phase 0 scan completed (298 files, hotspot ranking, CI-mapping gaps found) and paused for approval before Phase 1. Trail 192 agent finished two signed local branches (feat/collapse-by-relevance, measure/collapse-relevance-corpora) with passing checks, and the assistant began pushing and linking them.

repo: Dependency prop sources used to collapse past 30 props regardless of origin; the new rule in resolver/ambient.rs collapses only ambient sources (DOM/ARIA/style) past 30, plus any non-ambient source past 200 props as a size valve.
Storybook addon already runs with collapseInheritedProps: 'none', so collapse-rule changes do not affect it; only default CLI/NAPI output and agent consumers change.
3 Python test files (71 tests) are run by no CI job or just recipe.
The NAPI crate's own tests (11 #[test], 15 cfg(test) modules in crates/binding/src/lib.rs) are never run because every workflow/recipe passes --exclude caliper-docgen-napi.

Benchmark scripts use inconsistent extract invocations: bench.py uses --no-load-dependencies (not product default), weekly.py never passes --collapse-inherited-props, storybook-parity.mjs uses 'none' mostly.
Release and weekly workflows use jq `// empty` defaults, so a renamed JSON key would silently mean 'nothing to do'.
packages/napi/binding.d.ts is hand-synced with the Rust binding and must be updated manually.
Chakra v3 SystemProperties (705 props) is a style system under a name no ambient clause recognizes; the five design-system corpora treat it as project source, so only a consumer-app probe exposed it.

Largest real API source measured declares 75 props; layer records on tiny sources cost more bytes than the props they replace, so collapsing everything ambient regardless of size inflated shadcn to 441 layers.

code.finding: New ambient classifier (clauses 1-3: DOM file, DOM type name, style type name), pinned to the oracle's TS classifier by ambient_parity.json (628 verdicts); corpora exercise only 3 of 5 clauses.
collapses() now takes the type name so relevance can be decided per source; chain.rs has 7 allow attributes flagged by the scanner.
839 code lines with swallowed-panic risk and unrun inline tests; a Phase 3 candidate.

friction: Machine was heavily loaded throughout, widening spreads on lazy-session timings.
headline.py (PR #323) and layer_only_props.py (PR #324) were not on the agent's base, so the 'named only' headline bucket could not be measured.
Regex scanner overcounts: .ok() includes legitimate uses and doc-comment runs count as comment runs.
Phase 0 cannot cover docs (class 13), copied lists (class 5) or release-workflow strings (class 4); these need agent phases.
open_items: Awaiting user go-ahead for Phase 1 (about 8 Sonnet shards) and feedback on the Phase 3 module list (callisto-release.yml, cache.rs, resolver/mod.rs, discovery, binding/lib.rs).
Retarget measure/collapse-relevance-corpora to main once feat/collapse-by-relevance lands.
Larger Chakra consumer app not measured; the 3.8x figure is from four components.
Per-component cost of 'none' in a lazy Chakra-consumer session is unmeasured, relevant if the addon default is reconsidered.
Wire the 3 Python test files and the NAPI crate tests into CI.
Mantine and Spectrum pinned installs in /tmp/claude-501/t192/ are worth keeping for later runs.
